run.name: Skills Run 3: Progressive Learning Pilot
run.method: One agent transcribes all 5 manuscripts sequentially (easy→hard), receiving full evaluation + reference transcription after each. Agent maintains a living learning notebook that it rewrites between manuscripts. Alphabet-first method optional after MS1.
run.question: Does progressive learning with feedback between manuscripts improve transcription accuracy?
run.changes_from_baseline: Single agent doing all 5 manuscripts sequentially with evaluation feedback and reflection between each, rather than 5 independent agents per manuscript. Agent can freely revise its learning notebook.
run.note: Pilot run — single agent, not the standard 5-agent design. Results are not directly comparable to Runs 1-2 confidence intervals but can be compared to individual agent scores.

skill_version: SKILL.md v2 — positive framing with pen stroke test diagnostic (same as Run 2)

learning_trajectory.description: How the agent's behavior changed across 5 manuscripts
learning_trajectory.observation: Agent progressively increased use of uncertainty markers and gaps. Major shift at Brumwich (MS4) — possible over-correction toward gap-heavy strategy after receiving error feedback on 3 manuscripts.

top_suggestions: Confirmed sample alphabet from each scribe's hand (verify letter identifications)
Explicit two-pass approach (skeleton first, fill second)
More gradual difficulty progression (gap between MS3 and MS4 too large)
Stronger emphasis on vocab reference from the start
Word-level confidence scoring beyond binary confident/illegible
what_helped_most: Building alphabets from clear words before harder text
Learning to use [...] instead of guessing
agent_final_reflection.persistent_problem: Could not tell the difference between reading letterforms and unconsciously reconstructing from context. Self-awareness gap was biggest persistent issue.
agent_final_reflection.alphabet_decision: Built alphabet for all 5 manuscripts (only required for MS1). Adapted depth: 61-70 lines for legible, 25-38 for hard manuscripts. Never skipped the step.
